records.name: Run and Climb Club at Movement Fishtown
records.summary: A monthly group that runs a 5K route together and then climbs inside Movement Fishtown. The page says local runners and climbers are welcome, and runners of every level are invited.
records.what_you_do: Run a 5K route with the group, then spend the rest of the evening climbing at the gym.

schedule.text: Last Wednesday of every month at 6 pm

cost.text: $15 per person, free for Movement members

first_step.how: Check the Movement Fishtown events page for the current listing and price
first_step.basis: The page says runners of all levels are welcome and gives a posted price

records.notes: The events page is undated; its only year is in the footer, which is not used. No meeting spot beyond the gym is named. An older search snippet gave a 6:30 pm start, but the events page says 6 pm, so the page is followed.

records.name: BIPOC Night at Movement Fishtown
records.summary: A monthly evening at Movement Fishtown for Black, Indigenous and other people of color who climb, at any skill level.
records.what_you_do: Climb with other BIPOC climbers at the gym for an evening.

cost.text: $15 per person, free for Movement members

first_step.how: Check the Movement Fishtown events page for the current listing and price
first_step.basis: Open to climbers of all skill levels for a posted price

records.notes: BIPOC maps to five community ids (black, latino, asian_american, native_american, pacific_islander) because the cheatsheet has no BIPOC id. The events page is undated.

records.name: Women and Non-Binary Belay Alliance at Movement
records.summary: A monthly climbing night for women and nonbinary climbers at Movement. The page says it suits people who feel most at home in women's spaces.
records.what_you_do: Climb with other women and nonbinary climbers on a set monthly evening.

cost.text: $15 per person, free for Movement members

first_step.how: Check the Movement Fishtown events page for the current listing and price
first_step.basis: Open to the listed audience for a posted price

records.notes: The Fishtown events page lists this meetup at Movement Callowhill, which is where the location is recorded. Confirm the venue before going. The page includes nonbinary people, but the cheatsheet has no nonbinary community id, so only women is tagged. The events page is undated.

records.name: Bouldering Night at Tufas Boulder Lounge
records.summary: A free bouldering session at Tufas Boulder Lounge in Kensington, held on the first and third Tuesday of each month. Shoe rental is included, and a volunteer leads it.
records.what_you_do: Climb boulder problems, with shoes provided, for about two hours.

schedule.text: First and third Tuesday of the month, about 2 hours

first_step.how: Look up the next session on The Phoenix listing before you go

records.notes: The official Tufas site (tufas.com) redirects to a parked domain for sale, so The Phoenix listing is the only source. The listing shows the recurring pattern but no session date, and it reads Event Finished. A search snippet said newcomers are welcome, but the fetched page did not say so, so that is not recorded. Another Phoenix listing with the same Tufas text was tagged to Voorhees, NJ, and was not used. Confirm the next session before publishing.

records.name: Team Philly Race Training
records.summary: A paid season program for runners training for races, offered through Philadelphia Runner, the running store. Season memberships include weekly group runs, and race entries cost extra.
records.what_you_do: Train for a race with the group and join the weekly group runs that come with a season membership.

schedule.text: Weekly group runs come with a season membership. The program page does not list run days or times.

cost.text: 2026 season memberships: $125 spring, $150 fall half marathon, $175 fall full marathon, $250 full year. Race entries not included.

first_step.how: Buy a season membership on the RunSignup program page
first_step.basis: You need a paid season membership before you see the group runs

records.notes: This is a paid program, so the owner may want it outside a free or low cost list. Run days and meeting places appear only in older coverage (an October 2018 article and an undated residential listing), so they are not published. The program page gives the fall start as 8/1 in its description and 07/31 in the date range.

records.name: Women, Trans and Nonbinary Open Shop at Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A weekly evening open shop for women, trans and nonbinary adults who want to work on their own bikes with the shop's tools.
records.what_you_do: Work on your own bike at the shop with its tools during the open evening.

cost.text: Not listed for this night. The donation model described for Bike Church may also apply.

first_step.how: Come to 3939 Lancaster Ave on a Wednesday evening between 6:30 and 9 pm
first_step.basis: Set weekly hours open to the listed adults, with no sign-up described on the page

records.notes: The bike-shop page gives no dates for this program. One place on the page calls the Wednesday session Women/Trans/Non-Binary Only Bike Church shop hours. Nonbinary people are in the name, but the cheatsheet has no nonbinary community id, so only women and transgender are tagged.

records.name: Bike Church at Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: Adult do-it-yourself repair nights at Neighborhood Bike Works. You work on your own bike with the shop's tools and pay what you can.
records.what_you_do: Repair your own bike with the shop's tools, and do a quick chore while you are there.

schedule.text: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 6:30 to 9 pm, and the first Saturday of the month, 3 to 6 pm

first_step.how: Come to 3939 Lancaster Ave during the listed hours
first_step.basis: Open to adults 18 and up during set hours, with a pay what you can ask

records.notes: The page calls these hours both donation based and free DIY Bike Church hours, so the cost level may need a check. The page gives no year for any date. Mel's Community Bike Shop retail hours (Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 12 to 4 pm) are a shop, not a group, and are not recorded.

records.name: Ride Club at Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A free group ride class for kids and teens, ages 8 to 18, that meets on weekday afternoons in blocks of several weeks. A bike and helmet are provided for rides.
records.what_you_do: Learn group riding over several weeks and attend most classes to graduate.

schedule.text: Mondays and Wednesdays, or Tuesdays and Thursdays, 4 to 6 pm, in blocks of several weeks

cost.text: Free, with a $25 deposit that is refunded on completion

first_step.how: Contact the Director of Youth Programs by email (address on the youth programs page) to sign up
first_step.basis: Open to ages 8 to 18 with a stated deposit and a published contact. Riders must already be able to ride 20 minutes without a break.

records.notes: The youth page lists 2026 sessions, including one starting 9/7/2026, and a Saturday drop-in that restarts September 12, 2026. Graduates can move on to advanced programs, which are not recorded. The page gives no program address, so the shop address is shown. The director's email is included as published on the youth page.

records.name: Earn-a-Bike at Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A free bike repair class for kids and teens, ages 8 to 18. Students learn to fix bikes and get the chance to earn one.
records.what_you_do: Learn bike repair in a weekday afternoon class and get the chance to earn a bike.

schedule.text: Mondays and Wednesdays, or Tuesdays and Thursdays, 4 to 6 pm, in blocks of several weeks

cost.text: Free, with a $25 deposit that is refunded on completion

first_step.how: Contact the Director of Youth Programs by email (address on the youth programs page) to sign up
first_step.basis: Open to ages 8 to 18 with a stated deposit and a published contact

records.notes: The youth page lists an upcoming block from 10/5/2026 to 11/18/2026. The deposit is refunded on completion. Summer camp and advanced programs are not recorded.

notes:
Budget: all 3 WebSearch calls used (the cap), 33 WebFetch calls. Nine records published, none hidden or marked not_a_group. Verdict counts: publish 9.

Recorded: Neighborhood Bike Works (youth Ride Club and Earn-a-Bike, adult Bike Church, and the women, trans and nonbinary open shop); Movement Fishtown (Run and Climb Club, BIPOC Night, and the Women and Non-Binary Belay Alliance, which the events page lists at Movement Callowhill); the Tufas Boulder Lounge bouldering night as listed by The Phoenix, since tufas.com is parked; and Team Philly Race Training, which is a paid season program, so the owner may want to keep it out of a free or low cost list.

Checked, no record: Trophy Bikes has no weekly ride. Its one-time events are the Brommie Breakfast Roll (Sat 3/14, posted March 9, 2026, from Amtrak 30th Street Station, free) and the Bell Lap (July 3, 2025). Bicycle Therapy has no weekly ride; it sponsors race teams and helps with charity rides. Fleet Feet's store locator lists no Philadelphia store; the nearest is Springfield, PA. Movement Callowhill's Queer Climb Night is a single listing for Oct 8, 2026, 7 to 9 pm, with no repeat shown; the Fishtown events page says it is hosted by PHLash Climbing, which is already covered, so it is skipped. The Fishtown run-and-climb is taken from the gym's own events page, not from a search snippet that gave a 6:30 pm start and an April 29 date.

Not reached: Firth and Wilson (certificate error), Breakaway Bikes, Philly Bike Co-op, Bryn Mawr Running Company Philadelphia, and Philly Rock Gyms. The four guessed domains did not resolve, and the search budget ran out before I could look for their real sites. Search found only 2013 to 2017 listings for Breakaway and Firth and Wilson, and nothing current for Philly Bike Co-op, so none were recorded.

Not covered: yoga studios with community or donation classes. My slice names none and no search budget is left, so this needs its own search.

Dates: undated pages (the Movement events page, the Neighborhood Bike Works bike-shop page, and the Tufas listing) are marked probably_active with no sign-of-life month. The October 2018 residential-listing article is old evidence, so none of its run times are published. Team Philly's sign-of-life month comes from its 2026 RunSignup season listing.

Mapping: the cheatsheet has no BIPOC or nonbinary community id, so BIPOC Night uses five community ids, and the nonbinary groups tag only women and transgender where relevant. The director's email on the youth page is included as published.
